subject: Money
title: Railway Mania
description: A micro-lesson that makes Railway Mania usable.

hook.text: In the 1840s, Britain approved 9,500 miles of new railway. Only 6,220 miles were ever built. Investors lost billions.

buildup.text: Railways were transformative technology. Investors poured money into hundreds of competing railway companies.

discovery.text: Most routes were unprofitable. Too many companies served the same corridors, undercutting each other to death.

twist.text: The bubble bankrupted investors but left Britain with the world's best railway network. Destruction funded creation.

climax.text: The pattern repeats: transformative tech causes investment mania, a crash, then lasting infrastructure.

punchline.text: Wrong investors. Right technology. Great result.

quiz.question: What was the lasting result of railway mania?
